question.text: The force majeure clause in the legal documentation of Chambal Opportunities Fund was invoked during the COVID-19 pandemic. What is the effect of invoking a force majeure clause?

answer.text: All contractual obligations are permanently terminated
Performance of affected obligations is suspended or excused for the duration of the force majeure event, with obligations resuming once the event subsides
Only the fund manager's obligations are suspended; investor obligations continue
The fund immediately distributes all assets to investors

explanation.text: The Logic: In Indian contract law, invoking a force majeure clause typically suspends or excuses performance of the affected obligations for the duration of the qualifying event. Once the event subsides, the obligations resume. The clause does not permanently terminate contracts, does not apply one-sidedly to only the manager, and does not trigger immediate liquidation of the fund. The Trap: Permanent termination goes too far — force majeure provides temporary relief, not permanent termination. If the event is prolonged, separate termination provisions may apply. Note: The XIX-A workbook covers general legal/regulatory compliance and termination provisions in fund documents but does not specifically describe force-majeure mechanics or COVID-era invocations as a defined topic. Treat this as general contract-law knowledge applicable when reading AIF fund documents.
